# Benchmarks

```{r model_family_header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_header(
  family = "sdwba",
  pages = c(
    Overview = "index.html",
    Theory = "sdwba-theory.html",
    Implementation = "sdwba-implementation.html",
    Benchmarks = "sdwba-benchmarks.html",
    Validation = "sdwba-validation.html"
  )
)
```

SDWBA is benchmarked against the weakly scattering Jech et al. target set with fixed stochastic reference settings [@Jech_2015].

| Geometry | Max abs. $\Delta$ vs benchmark (dB) | Mean abs. $\Delta$ vs benchmark (dB) | Elapsed (s) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Weakly scattering sphere | 10.08475 | 0.35609 | 0.72 |
| Weakly scattering prolate spheroid | 2.05918 | 0.07638 | 3.58 |
| Weakly scattering cylinder | 2.07406 | 0.15895 | 1.91 |

Increasing `n_iterations` stabilizes the stochastic ensemble estimate, but it does not force the stochastic approximation onto the deterministic modal-series benchmark.

## Stochastic krill software-reference comparisons

The stochastic krill benchmark uses matched segment geometry, orientation, ensemble settings, and frequency grid for the published krill reference case [@CCAMLR_SDWBA_software; @NOAA_SDWBA_software]. These are software-reference comparisons, so they are reported as benchmarks.

| Comparison | Mean abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) | Max abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) |
|:--|--:|--:|
| acousticTS vs stochastic reference A | 0.06978 | 0.18270 |
| acousticTS vs stochastic reference B | 0.06158 | 0.52846 |
| Reference A vs reference B | 0.13036 | 0.65798 |

::: {.note data-title="Stochastic convention"}
Report SDWBA benchmark residuals with the stochastic settings. Different phase conventions can produce visibly different curves while preserving the same broad approximation regime.
:::
